standard_prerequisites.name: Soundness of schemas
standard_prerequisites.statement: If a relation R has one of the listed properties (serial, reflexive, symmetric, transitive, euclidean), every instance of the corresponding axiom schema (D, T, B, 4, 5) is true in every model with that relation (thm:soundschemas, sibling frame-definability unit).
standard_prerequisites.use: Opens the proof: all instances of T and B are true in every reflexive symmetric model, so by soundness a countermodel need only invalidate one instance of 4 (and of 5).

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1561-1563): KTB proves neither 4 (Box p implies Box Box p) nor 5 (Diamond not-p implies Box Diamond not-p).

Reduction (proof lines 1566-1571): by the soundness-of-schemas theorem all T and B instances hold in reflexive symmetric models; by soundness it suffices to exhibit a reflexive symmetric model with a world falsifying an instance of 4, and similarly for 5; the same model serves both claims.

Countermodel evaluation (proof lines 1571-1575): in the reflexive symmetric model of fig:KTBnot45 (delivered as context span, lines 1578-1599) the formula Box p implies Box Box p fails at w1, so axiom 4 fails; and Diamond not-p implies Box Diamond not-p fails at w2, so the instance of 5 with A = not-p fails.
proof_roadmap: Reduce by soundness to exhibiting a reflexive symmetric countermodel.
Read the two-world symmetric reflexive model from the delivered figure.
Evaluate the 4 instance at w1 and the 5 instance at w2 to conclude both failures.
difficulty_reason: Non-provability by countermodel (statement 1561-1563, proof 1565-1576): soundness reduction plus explicit evaluation of both failing instances at named worlds of the delivered figure; the figure is load-bearing and enters as a context span. H2.
